items.q: Then I started playing with Duke Ellington and he never really said too much like that.

ctx.x: Did your parents, like were they supportive?

Do they worry and do they still worry? My father always used to say to me, “When are you going to go back to school?” “When are you going to get a haircut.” Right? Then I started playing with Duke Ellington and he never really said too much like that. It was some years after that when I was back in New York. I was really into math and I went as far as calculus in high school and I really loved it. I love using that part of my mind. So about ten years later I decided to take a class at the New School in calculus…
Whoa. He came around. Yeah. Well your weekly — a week for you, I can imagine every day is like a little different. Right.

items.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I’m very lucky, I played with Stevie Wonder, Duke Ellington, B.B. King, other black groups you know?

ctx.x: Well, as I told you earlier, my wife who is also a Caucasian from Norway, who has never seen anything like this except on the news, and she doesn’t want to march, and I understand it because it’s really dangerous with the virus too, and I’ve got my feelings about that, I’m not sure, but she worked on it yesterday and she came home and told me, and she’s a bit shy, she gave me an idea that she wanted me to initiate, and I would have initiated it but I really wanted her to. She said, “Let’s call up all our black or…
Yeah, we have a path sort of.
